title: QUIC protocol error with Chrome-based browsers
body:
### Detailed Description of the Problem

On our dev environment, where we have QUIC enabled, we regularly get images failing to be served on Chromium-based browsers, with the `net::ERR_QUIC_PROTOCOL_ERROR 200` error code.

This eventually makes the browser refuse to use QUIC with our origin for a while as well.

Obviously this isn't a lot of information to go off of, so I included some quic traces (see below).

### Expected Behavior

No error

### Steps to Reproduce the Behavior

Not entirely clear at this stage.

Our best reproducer so far is to load a page full of images (doesn't seem to happen regularly with plain HTML and other smaller payloads). Such a way we can reproduce it on our dev environment is as follows:
1. Start chromium forcing QUIC to the origin: `chromium-browser --enable-quic --origin-to-force-quic-on=<redacted-host>:443`
1. Accessing a page with a lot of images, like https://<redacted-host>/titles
2. Set the view mode to grid so larger (& thus bigger) thumbnails are loaded
![2023-01-18 10_50_19](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/875533/213152658-067cd16c-0bef-4420-932b-443394896bbb.png)
3. Go to the next page until it happens (pagination at the bottom, usually I hit it after 1 or 2 pages only)

Note: if you try to repro, use the pagination for new images, rather than disabling the browser cache and refreshing the page, JS assets loading spam will get you rate-limited after a few refreshes otherwise due to a bug in our dev environment rate-limiting config.

### Do you have any idea what may have caused this?

_No response_

### Do you have an idea how to solve the issue?

_No response_

### What is your configuration?

### Additional Information

Attached is a QUIC developer trace around one such event

[haproxy-quic-protocol-error-1117.gz](https://github.com/haproxy/haproxy/files/10445324/haproxy-quic-protocol-error-1117.gz)

It *might* be loosely related to a backend exhibiting symptoms of https://github.com/haproxy/haproxy/issues/1992 . In this case, the images are proxy-cached by nginx from our prod, which is running 2.7.1 and thus affected by it (until a 2.7.2 bundling it is issued). Without forcing the origin, the browser will downgrade from QUIC to H2, and you'll get those instead of the QUIC errors. On one hand you could say we should try with prod on 2.8-dev + that fix, but on the other hand it's rather odd for haproxy to be affected like that by a faulty backend (even if it's nginx->haproxy in that case).

Though to be completely honest that one occasional quic error has been happening for a while, so it might be a coincidence and go way back.

Another interesting aspect is that the browser eventually retries the H3 request and gets a 206 back (from nginx's cache in such cases). Maybe ranges responses are somehow not very nicely handled. Hard to say.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Hello,  error 200 QUIC error protocol looks like the h3 application error code H3_NO_ERROR meaning "no error".

About the traces, I would like to know if you stripped some information. The transport parameters (TP) traces are missing. I ask that because there are suspect trace for 0x78657805b410 QUIC connection (without TP dump). haproxy received the last 1RTT here without any remaining packet in flight:

<0>2023-01-18T11:17:11.617894+00:00 [02|quic|2|c_conn.c:2777] RX frame : qc@participant4 frm@participant5 PADDING

Then after about 60s of inactivity it closes only the mux:

<0>2023-01-18T11:17:12.608935+00:00 [02|quic|5|prt_quic.c:26] quic_close(): entering : qc@participant4
<0>2023-01-18T11:17:12.608953+00:00 [02|quic|5|c_conn.c:1599] qc_check_close_on_released_mux(): entering : qc@participant4
<0>2023-01-18T11:17:12.608955+00:00 [02|quic|5|c_conn.c:1607] qc_check_close_on_released_mux(): leaving : qc@participant4
<0>2023-01-18T11:17:12.608957+00:00 [02|quic|5|prt_quic.c:39] quic_close(): leaving : qc@participant4

A few minutes later:

<0>2023-01-18T11:17:18.283501+00:00 [02|quic|5|c_conn.c:5801] retrieve_qc_conn_from_cid(): entering
<0>2023-01-18T11:17:18.283508+00:00 [02|quic|5|c_conn.c:5837] retrieve_qc_conn_from_cid(): leaving : qc@participant4 err_code=0x100

haproxy set its application error code to H3_NO_ERROR.

Then haproxy receives new STREAM frames. As the connection is not released contrary to the mux haproxy sends STOP_SENDING for STREAM it receives new data. Even for h3 Control Stream with 10 as ID which is a unidirectional stream open by the client if I remember well.

Chrome does not seems happy to receive such a STOP_SENDING for the h3 Control stream:

<0>2023-01-18T11:17:18.293377+00:00 [02|quic|2|c_conn.c:2777] RX frame : qc@participant4 frm@participant5 CONNECTION_CLOSE_APP error_code=260 reason_phrase_len=47 reason_phrase: '156:STOP_SENDING received for QPACK send stream'

Error 260 is this one about the h3 RFC:

`H3_CLOSED_CRITICAL_STREAM (0x104):  A stream required by the HTTP/3
      connection was closed or reset.`

About h3 Control streams:

`
6.2.1 Control streams
The
   sender MUST NOT close the control stream, and the receiver MUST NOT
   request that the sender close the control stream.
`
I do not know if such an error may lead the client to never come back.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: To me we should at least modify our code to never send STOP_SENDING frames for h3 Control stream.

I did not have much time to work on this issue and it's not easy to understand chrome behavior as I failed in reproduce the issue locally with web services on my own.

Regarding the stalled requests, maybe this is caused due to a recent regression which prevent the H3 GOAWAY emission. I merged a fix for this in the master branch so you may perform a new test it with the previous patch applied.

If you still have issue, you can replace the patch by the new version provided in this comment. This is refined version with `RESET_STREAM` sent under certain condition instead of an empty STREAM with FIN set. This is experimental as it's not easy to test these conditions.

comments.body:
In other news, running 2.8-dev ( d85227fca20a5c793857c1632283ef4a2120285a ) I get some QUIC protocol errors.

![2023-02-07 23_08_42](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/875533/217387817-9cad0fe5-2edc-4050-a302-c7c96c81ce17.png)

But the good news is that I triggered those while setting up a reproducer for this issue as a whole

Here's the hacky configuration I came to https://github.com/reporter/haproxy-bug-repros/blob/issue-2004/haproxy.cfg

Unfortunately it's a bit tricky to even run correctly without accidentally having some H2 fallbacks triggering left and right...

You need to ensure the following:
1. You're using the local haproxy as an entrypoint (some /etc/hosts editing should do the trick)
2. You're forcing H3 etc on chrome (`chromium-browser --ignore-certificate-errors --enable-quic --origin-to-force-quic-on=localhost:443 --origin-to-force-quic-on=<redacted-host>:443 --origin-to-force-quic-on=<redacted-host>:443` is my complete CLI command)
3. You can then access https://localhost which should load a proxied copy of our dev website

Probably you'll run into QUIC issues. But maybe not either. If not, then I have no good repro. I merely see it happen on 50% of chrome sessions; sometimes entirely breaking, sometimes images, sometimes working flawlessly. Hard to say for sure tbh...
